clue.text: Among the servants in the basement

definitions.meaning: in the domestic staff's world of a grand house
on the floor beneath ground level

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both in the servants' quarters and down on the lowest floor of a house.

clue.text: Despite the arrears endorse the ship's record

parts.note: to endorse a plan is to back it
a log is the official daily record kept aboard a ship

explanation.surface: Someone backs a ship's record even though there are debts outstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Despite the' is only a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile of unfinished work or unpaid bills is an accumulation of arrears.

clue.text: Grounds holding large number in West Yorkshire

indicators.note: the grounds word holds the number inside it, the way a container grips its contents

parts.note: grounds, as in coffee grounds, are dregs or lees
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number

explanation.surface: Somewhere in West Yorkshire a sports ground accommodates a big crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' suggests football pitches but means dregs. The definition is loose: the city stands for its county.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the largest settlement in the county of West Yorkshire.

clue.text: Arranged to get a new vehicle

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put into a fresh order here

explanation.surface: Something was set up so that someone could acquire a new car.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagonette is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, a vehicle with side seats facing each other.

clue.text: Egotistical dedication of a book

definitions.meaning: a book dedicated by its author to himself would say these two words

explanation.definitionFit: A vain inscription reads 'to me', and a tome is a big weighty volume.

clue.text: The insinuation is that union members go round corrupting Ned

indicators.note: the scrambled union letters surround the scrambled name, so they go round it
the members of union are its constituent letters, here rearranged
corrupting the name Ned spoils its letter order

explanation.surface: A rumour spreads that trade unionists are leading a man named Ned astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' is unusual: it treats the word union as a set of letters to be shuffled, the sort of loose signal older puzzles allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an indirect hint or suggestion, typically a disparaging one.

clue.text: Post bet

definitions.meaning: a pointed wooden pole driven into the ground

explanation.definitionFit: A stake is both a wooden post and the sum put at risk on a wager.

clue.text: Time for the bowler-and not before time!

definitions.meaning: in cricket an over is the bowler's turn of six balls, so the over being due means it is time for the bowler
late, arriving after it was expected

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means a cricket over is owed to the bowler; as one it means late.

clue.text: Shrink from making an agreement

definitions.meaning: to get smaller or draw together

explanation.definitionFit: Muscles contract when they shrink, and a contract is a formal legal agreement.

clue.text: He works in cloth-but isn't a tailor

definitions.text: He works in cloth-but isn't a tailor

parts.words: He works in cloth-but isn't a tailor
parts.note: the cloth is the clerical profession, so a man of the cloth works in it without sewing anything

explanation.definitionFit: Priests are called men of the cloth, after their distinctive dress.

clue.text: Jack takes poem home

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB is an able seaman
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A sailor brings a poem back to his house.
explanation.definitionFit: An abode is a dwelling place, where someone lives.

clue.text: See Carol going down!

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
to carol is to sing joyfully

explanation.surface: Watch a woman named Carol descend.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol looks like a woman's name but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A team that is going down in a match is on the way to defeat.

clue.text: Nest rebuilt in a rush was not favourably received

indicators.note: the rebuilt nest sits inside the plant word

parts.note: a rush is a reed-like waterside plant

indicators.note: rebuilt means the letters of nest are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A bird's nest remade among the reeds got a cool reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' turns NEST into SENT, which goes 'in' REED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resented was taken with bitterness or indignation rather than welcomed.

clue.text: Arrive at hospital in slum area

indicators.note: the hospital letter is placed inside the phrase for arriving

parts.note: to arrive at a place is to get to it
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone reaches a hospital in a deprived district.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghetto is a poor, overcrowded part of a city occupied by a minority group.

clue.text: Ten I possibly rely on completely

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: I might count on ten things entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges TEN I into ENTI; 'on' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Entirely and completely both mean wholly, to the full extent.

clue.text: Enough now to compare

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era, so it stands for now
to equate things is to compare them as equal

explanation.surface: That is now sufficient to make a comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: Adequate means sufficient, as much as is needed.

clue.text: The current price for a Shakespearean extract perhaps

definitions.meaning: a stated price quoted for goods or work
a passage cited from a play, for instance

explanation.definitionFit: A builder's quote is an estimated cost; a line cited from Hamlet is a citation from literature.

clue.text: In favour of a lock for the stronghold

parts.note: to be for something is to be in favour of it
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone argues that a lock is needed for the castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a door's fastening but means a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A stronghold is a fortified place such as a castle.

clue.text: How bounders are caught unawares?

parts.note: bounders read as leaping creatures are caught mid-jump, unprepared

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means caught unprepared or by surprise, imagined literally as catching a jumper mid-leap.

clue.text: A place of prayer or eloquent speaking

definitions.meaning: a small chapel for private worship

explanation.definitionFit: An oratory is a small chapel, and oratory is skilful rhetoric.

clue.text: One able to carry his drink?

definitions.meaning: a dark beer brewed from roasted malt

explanation.definitionFit: A railway luggage carrier and a dark stout share the name; the joke is a man holding his liquor.

clue.text: Lionhearted king, one in church uncompromising

indicators.note: the numeral for one sits inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: RC is the Roman Catholic church
I is the Roman numeral one
hard means unbending or uncompromising

explanation.surface: A brave monarch is a stern man at church.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard I of England was nicknamed Coeur de Lion, the Lionheart.

clue.text: Actor hams it on the Fourth of July-a heinous act

indicators.note: an actor who hams overacts, mangling the performance and so the letters
the fourth letter of July is picked out

explanation.surface: A ham actor's dreadful Independence Day performance is a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hams' rearranges ACTOR into ATROC; IT is as written; 'Fourth of July' is not the holiday but its fourth letter, and 'on' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrocity is an appalling, wicked deed.

clue.text: Was concerned about a revolutionary

parts.note: CA is circa, Latin for about
a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: Someone worried over a radical agitator.
explanation.definitionFit: To have cared is to have felt worry or concern.

clue.text: Jack turns to lieutenant in charge of Northern sea

indicators.note: turns means the sailor's letters face the other way

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor turns to his officer commanding a northern sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' makes BA from AB; 'to' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic is the sea of northern Europe between Scandinavia and the continent.

clue.text: Follow the track

explanation.definitionFit: To trail someone is to follow them, and a trail is a path.

clue.text: Mark left on Sam's first vehicle

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of the word Sam's

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Sam's first car got a dent.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left on skin after a wound heals.

clue.text: Tanker's water heater will not start

indicators.note: the heater word loses its starting letter

parts.note: a boiler heats water

explanation.surface: A tanker's boiler refuses to fire up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanker's' is Tanker is: an oiler is a tanker carrying oil.
explanation.definitionFit: An oiler is a ship that carries oil, a type of tanker.

clue.text: Chilean ad another Mexican dish

indicators.note: another signals a different version of these letters

explanation.surface: A Chilean advert features yet another Mexican dish.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a tortilla rolled round a filling and baked in chilli sauce, a Mexican dish.

clue.text: Put out when Di's led round by a pig, we hear!

indicators.note: the words Di's led go round the pig's noise

parts.note: taken as written
a grunt is the noise heard from a pig

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed when Diana is led about by a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' is not a homophone signal: it says GRUNT is the pig's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Disgruntled means annoyed, put out, the way someone is when offended.
